*The Force Awakens* premiered in Hollywood, Los Angeles, on December 14, 2015, and was released in the United States on December 18. It was positively received by critics, who found it an action-packed film with the mix of new and familiar actors capturing the nostalgia of the original trilogy and giving the franchise new energy.[4] The film grossed $2.07 billion worldwide, breaking various box office records and becoming the highest-grossing film in the United States and Canada, the highest-grossing film of 2015, and the third-highest-grossing film at the time of its release. It was nominated for five awards at the 88th Academy Awards, and received numerous other accolades. The film was followed by *The Last Jedi* (2017) and *The Rise of Skywalker* (2019), rounding out the *Star Wars* sequel trilogy.

The film was announced after The Walt Disney Company's acquisition of Lucasfilm in October 2012. The film is the first *Star Wars* film to not extensively involve franchise creator George Lucas, who only served as a creative consultant in the early stages of production. *The Force Awakens* was produced by Abrams, his longtime collaborator Bryan Burk, and Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy. Abrams and Lawrence Kasdan, co-writer of the original trilogy films *The Empire Strikes Back* (1980) and *Return of the Jedi*, rewrote an initial script by Michael Arndt. John Williams, composer for the previous episodic films, returned to compose the score. Principal photography began in April 2014 and concluded the following November. Filming took place on sets at Pinewood Studios in England, and on location mainly in Abu Dhabi, Iceland, and Ireland. On a budget of $447 million, it is the most expensive film ever made.

*Star Wars: The Last Jedi* grossed $620.2 million in the United States and Canada, and $712.5 million in other territories, for a worldwide total of $1.333 billion.[3] It was the highest-grossing film of 2017 and the ninth-highest-grossing film of all time.[81][82] The film had a worldwide opening of $450.8 million, the eighth-biggest of all time, including $40.6 million that was attributed to IMAX screenings, the second biggest for IMAX.[83][84] It was estimated that the film would need to gross $800 million worldwide to break even;[85] On December 31, 2017, the film crossed the $1 billion mark,[86] making it the third *Star Wars* film to do so. *Deadline Hollywood* calculated the film's net profit as $417.5 million, accounting for production budgets, marketing, talent participations, and other costs; box office grosses and home media revenues placed it first on their list of 2017's "Most Valuable Blockbusters".[87]

The film had its world premiere at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles on December 9, 2017,[74] and was released in the United States on December 15,[75] in IMAX and 3D.[76][77] The film was originally scheduled to be released in the United States on May 26;[78] however, it was pushed back to December to avoid competition with *Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales* (2017).[75]



### Home media

[edit]

Walt Disney Studios Home Entertainment released *Star Wars: The Last Jedi* digitally in HD and 4K via digital download and Movies Anywhere on March 13, 2018, with an Ultra HD Blu-ray, Blu-ray, and DVD physical release on March 27.[79] On March 31, 2020, a 27-disc Skywalker Saga box set was released, containing all nine films in the series, with each film receiving three discs, a Blu-ray version, a 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray, and special features found on the 2011 release for the first six episodic films.[80]



## Reception

[edit]

### Box office

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>
Pre-sale tickets went on sale in the United States on October 9, 2017, and as with *The Force Awakens* and *Rogue One*, ticket service sites such as Fandango had their servers crash due to heavy traffic and demand.[88] In the United States and Canada, industry tracking had *The Last Jedi* grossing around $200 million from 4,232 theaters in its opening weekend.[89][90] The film made $45 million from Thursday night previews, the second-highest amount ever (behind *The Force Awakens*' $57 million).[91] It went on to make $104.8 million on its first day (including previews), and $220 million over the weekend, both the second-highest amounts of all time.[89] The opening weekend figure included an IMAX opening-weekend of $25 million, the biggest IMAX opening of the year, and the second biggest ever behind *The Force Awakens*.[92]

## Plot

[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

In January 2015, Disney CEO Bob Iger stated that *Episode VIII* would be released in 2017.[29] In December, Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy said that the film had not been mapped out and that Abrams was collaborating with Johnson, who would in turn work with (then) *Episode IX* director Colin Trevorrow to ensure a smooth transition.[30] Additionally, Abrams served as an executive producer along with Tom Karnowski and Jason McGatlin.[16] In January 2017, Lucasfilm announced the title for *Episode VIII* as *Star Wars: The Last Jedi*.[31]



### Writing

[edit]

The *Last Jedi* story begins immediately after *The Force Awakens*.[32] Johnson had his story group watch films such as *Twelve O'Clock High* (1949), *The Bridge on the River Kwai* (1957), *Gunga Din* (1939), *Three Outlaw Samurai* (1964), *Sahara* (1943), and *Letter Never Sent* (1960) for inspiration while developing ideas.[32][33] He felt it was difficult to work on the film while *The Force Awakens* was being finished.[32]

***Star Wars: The Last Jedi*** (also known as ***Star Wars: Episode VIII – The Last Jedi***) is a 2017 American epic space opera film written and directed by Rian Johnson. Produced by Lucasfilm and distributed by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, it is the second installment of the *Star Wars* sequel trilogy, following *The Force Awakens* (2015), and the eighth episode of the nine-part "Skywalker saga". The film's ensemble cast includes Mark Hamill, Carrie Fisher, Adam Driver, Daisy Ridley, John Boyega, Oscar Isaac, Andy Serkis, Lupita Nyong'o, Domhnall Gleeson, Anthony Daniels, Gwendoline Christie, Kelly Marie Tran, Laura Dern, and Benicio del Toro. *The Last Jedi* follows Rey as she seeks the aid of Luke Skywalker in hopes of turning the tide for the Resistance in the fight against Kylo Ren and the First Order while General Leia Organa, Finn, and Poe Dameron attempt to escape a First Order attack on the dwindling Resistance fleet.

In July 2013, Kennedy confirmed at the *Star Wars* Celebration Europe that John Williams would return to score the *Star Wars* sequel trilogy.[62][63] Williams confirmed his assignment for *The Last Jedi* at a Tanglewood concert in August 2016,[64] stating he would begin recording the score "off and on" in December 2016 until March or April 2017.[65] On February 21, 2017, it was confirmed that recording was underway, with both Williams and William Ross conducting the sessions.[66][16] In lieu of a traditional spotting session with Johnson, Williams was provided a temp track of music from his previous film scores as a reference for scoring *The Last Jedi*.[67] The official soundtrack album was released by Walt Disney Records on December 15, 2017.[68]

User-generated scores at Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic received considerable coverage for being more negative. Audience scores on such sites require only registration and do not ensure that contributing voters have seen the film.[121] Several reviewers speculated that coordinated vote brigading from internet groups and bots contributed to the low scores,[122][123] including analysis provided by *Quartz* and Bleeding Cool.[124][125] After initially rejecting tampering claims,[126] Rotten Tomatoes later said in 2019 that *The Last Jedi* had been "seriously targeted" by a review-bombing campaign.[127] Scott Mendelson of *Forbes* labeled the negative reaction "alleged", saying it was based on "easily trolled online user polls", and he criticized Disney for placating the "vocal minority" in its approach to the sequel, *The Rise of Skywalker*.[128]

In January 2016, production of *Episode VIII* was delayed until February due to script rewrites.[45] Filming was in danger of being delayed further due to an upcoming strike between the Producers Alliance for Cinema and Television and the Broadcasting, Entertainment, Cinematograph and Theatre Union.[46] On February 10, 2016, Disney CEO Bob Iger confirmed that principal photography had begun[47] under the working title *Space Bear*.[32] Additional filming took place in Dubrovnik, Croatia from March 9 to 16,[48][49] as well as in Ireland in May.[50] Malin Head in County Donegal and a mountain headland, Ceann Sibeal in County Kerry, served as additional filming locations.[51] To increase the scenes' intimacy Driver and Ridley were both present when filming Kylo and Rey's Force visions.[52] Location filming for the battle scenes on the planet Crait took place at the Salar de Uyuni salt flats in Bolivia.[53] Additional filming took place in Mexico.[54]

*The Last Jedi* was also characterized by reviewers as divisive among audiences.[129] Emily VanDerWerff of *Vox* found that dissatisfied fans saw the film as too progressive, disliked its humor, plot, or character arcs, or felt betrayed that it ignored fan theories.[122] Other reviewers made similar observations.[130] Particularly divisive was the reveal that Rey's parents are insignificant;[131] many fans had expected her to be Luke's daughter or to share a lineage with another character from the original trilogy.[132] There was also sentiment that Snoke's character was underdeveloped and that Luke's actions contradicted his previous heroic portrayal.[133] Reviewers claimed that fan theories were held so strongly among some viewers that it was difficult for them to accept different stories,[134] but they noted that other viewers appreciated the film's action, tone, and deviation from *Star Wars* tradition.[135][136]

It received mixed reviews from critics and grossed over $1.077 billion worldwide, making it the seventh-highest-grossing film of 2019; although it was the lowest-grossing installment of the trilogy, it turned an estimated net profit of $300 million (with an assumed production budget of $275 million; the true $416 million budget would decrease profits to $150 million).[7] It received three nominations at the 92nd Academy Awards (Best Original Score, Best Visual Effects, and Best Sound Editing) as well as three at the 73rd British Academy Film Awards (also Best Special Visual Effects, Best Original Music, and Best Sound). It won five awards at the 46th Saturn Awards, including Best Science Fiction Film.

Based on my Wikipedia searches, I've found detailed box office breakdowns for both Star Wars films. Here's the comprehensive information you requested:

## **Star Wars: Episode VIII - The Last Jedi (2017)**

### **Box Office Totals:**
- **Domestic (U.S./Canada):** $620.2 million
- **International (overseas):** $712.5 million  
- **Worldwide Total:** $1.333 billion

### **Performance Context & Rankings:**
- **Highest-grossing film of 2017** globally
- **Ninth-highest-grossing film of all time** at the time of its run
- **Second-highest-grossing Star Wars film** (behind The Force Awakens)
- **Third Star Wars film to cross $1 billion worldwide**

### **Opening Weekend Records & Milestones:**
- **Domestic opening weekend:** $220 million (second-highest of all time at release)
- **Thursday night previews:** $45 million (second-highest ever behind The Force Awakens' $57 million)
- **Opening day total:** $104.8 million (including previews, second-highest ever)
- **Worldwide opening:** $450.8 million (eighth-biggest of all time)
- **IMAX performance:** $25 million opening weekend (biggest IMAX opening of 2017, second-biggest ever)
- **IMAX worldwide:** $40.6 million attributed to IMAX screenings (second-biggest for IMAX)

### **Additional Context:**
- Net profit calculated at **$417.5 million** by Deadline Hollywood
- Estimated to need **$800 million worldwide** to break even (far exceeded)
- Crossed **$1 billion mark on December 31, 2017**
- Set all-time opening weekend records in multiple countries (France, Germany, Spain, UK, Finland)
- Became the **fourth-highest-grossing film of 2017 in Europe** by its second weekend

---

## **Star Wars: Episode IX - The Rise of Skywalker (2019)**

### **Box Office Totals:**
- **Domestic (U.S./Canada):** $515.2 million
- **International (overseas):** $561.8 million  
- **Worldwide Total:** $1.077 billion

### **Performance Context & Rankings:**
- **Seventh-highest-grossing film of 2019**
- **Lowest-grossing installment of the sequel trilogy** (below The Force Awakens and The Last Jedi)
- **Crossed $1 billion mark on January 14, 2020** (became Disney's seventh 2019 film to do so)
- **Third highest-grossing film of 2019 in the U.S.** (behind Avengers: Endgame and The Lion King)

### **Opening Weekend Records & Milestones:**
- **Domestic opening weekend:** $177.4 million (third-highest December opening ever)
- **12th-best domestic opening of all time** (at release)
- **Opening day total:** $89.6 million (including $40 million from Thursday previews)
- **Thursday previews:** $40 million (sixth-highest opening day total of all time)
- **Christmas Day performance:** $32 million (second-best Christmas Day total ever, behind The Force Awakens' $49.3 million)
- **Worldwide opening:** $373.5 million (below projections, 47% lower than The Last Jedi)

### **Additional Context:**
- Net profit estimated at **$300 million** (lowest of the Disney trilogy titles)
- **Production budget:** $416 million (third most expensive film ever made)
- **Atom Tickets second-best first-day seller** of all time behind Endgame
- **Fandango reported it outsold all previous Star Wars films** in advance sales
- **CinemaScore:** B+ (lowest of the sequel trilogy)
- Largest international markets: UK ($26.8M), Germany ($21.8M), France ($15.2M), Japan ($14.6M), Australia ($12.6M)

### **Notable Performance Factors:**
- Opening weekend was affected by **Saturday being the busiest shopping day of the year**
- **China performance:** Only $12.1 million total (significant underperformance)
- **46% drop from Friday to Saturday** during opening weekend (unusual for major franchises)

This data shows The Last Jedi significantly outperformed The Rise of Skywalker both domestically and internationally, with The Last Jedi achieving stronger opening records and overall box office performance despite being the middle film of the trilogy.
